title: Telemetry-to-Response Adaptor: Enriched Handoff for PagerDuty & Slack
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a telemetry->response adaptor that synthesizes traces, metric slices, and focused log excerpts into a compact evidence bundle attached to PagerDuty incidents and Slack incident threads. This adaptor should enable on-call engineers to understand the failure surface in <60s, provide one-click runbook links, and seed an auto-generated postmortem draft when incidents are marked resolved.

Scope:
- Trace hooks: sampling and gated extraction of top-N spans, span annotations, and key KV cache hot-path markers.
- Metric/log pipeline enrichments: time-windowed metric deltas (p95/p99 slices), anomaly flags, and log highlight snippets filtered by error signatures.
- Attachment packaging: deterministic evidence bundle format (compact JSON+compressed logs) consumable by Slack blocks and PagerDuty attachments.
- Postmortem seed: short incident summary, timeline of key events (first-error, mitigation, rollback), and suggested RCA checklist items.
- Controls: toggles per-customer (Private/Dedicated/Hosted), RBAC forwarding rules, and sampling budgets to avoid unbounded storage/ingress costs.

Non-goals: full NLP root-cause inference, replacing operator judgment, or running heavyweight ML summarizers inline on critical path. For now, summarization is optional async job after incident creation.
acceptance_criteria: PD incident created with attached evidence bundle containing: 3 trace snippets, metric p95/p99 delta chart URL, and 10-line log highlights
Slack incident thread receives rich attachment with one-click runbook links and quick-actions (acknowledge, create postmortem draft)
Postmortem draft generator creates a markdown scaffold in the incidents Confluence space pre-populated with timeline and links
Sampling budget respected under burst traffic: adaptor does not increase ingestion cost by >5% for an average customer during a 1-hour outage
Feature gates allow disabling attachments for Private deployments and enforce RBAC controls

comments: 2026-02-04 — Asha: Kickoff notes — scoped adaptor to an evidence-bundle format to avoid heavy inline summarization. Shared initial Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Telemetry-to-Response-Adaptor

2026-02-14 — Diego: Implemented first PoC for span selector. Uses weighted-span scoring (error flag, latency delta, sampled-by) and extracts top-3 spans. Observed ~12ms additional latency when triggered — acceptable for async attach path.
2026-02-20 — Mark: Slack template v1 uploaded. Need design feedback on compactness and mobile rendering; flagged issue where attachments truncate long trace IDs. Filed UI task DES-501.
2026-02-28 — Lina: Metrics delta generator blocked by metrics infra quota increase. Opened ENG-412820 to request quota bump; estimate 2 days after approval.

2026-03-05 — Security review request created. SRE warns about potential leakage of PII in logs; plan to apply log scrubber rules and configurable redaction. Security reviewer: 'require explicit opt-in for customer logs export' — acknowledged.
2026-03-08 — Diego: Started integration with PagerDuty Events V2 attachment API. Noted limit of 100KB per attachment; switched to compressed bundle with link fallback to storage for >100KB bundles.

2026-03-10 — Priya: Postmortem scaffold finalized — template includes timeline, evidence bundle links, mitigation steps, and impacted customers list. Confluence API token rotation planned with infra team.
progress_and_decisions: Decision: evidence bundle will be asynchronous attach (non-blocking) to avoid latency impact on request path
Tradeoff: richer summarization deferred to async job to keep initial rollout simple and cost-predictable
Fallback: if bundle exceeds PD/Slack size limits, upload compressed artifact to secure object store and attach link; ensure link TTL and auth enforcement
Rollout plan: feature-flagged release to internal accounts -> beta customers -> all hosted customers; Private deployments disabled by default until RBAC validation
Monitoring: add SLOs for attach success rate, bundle generation latency, and storage costs per-incident
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: sensitive data exfiltration via log snippets — Mitigation: strict scrubber rules, manual allowlist per-customer, and security sign-off required before enabling for Private deployments
Risk: unbounded cost due to large bundles during mass incidents — Mitigation: sampling budgets, compression and link fallback, and daily cost alerts
Risk: PagerDuty/Slack API rate limits — Mitigation: batching adaptor calls and exponential backoff with queueing and dead-letter handling
